PUBLIC-DOC.rule: A named release reference/guide API directive or release-selected autosummary entry establishes a documented public contract/view unless positive explicit internal-only evidence applies. This proves contract existence, not complete semantics, runtime availability or implementation.

PUBLIC-EXPORT.rule: Literal public __all__ export selected by a documented automodule is a public export. Retain its obligation while detailed documented semantics, generated selection and variant contracts remain to be reviewed.

ALIAS-VIEW.rule: An explicit source import/assignment alias, protocol pseudo-class declaration, unqualified guide spelling or lexically scoped C member is a source-backed view. Retain public variants and source IDs; do not infer whole-domain equivalence, runtime alias identity or deduplicated capability count from a view.

PRIVATE-POSITIVE.rule: Only the exact internally-used-structures section's explicitly named declarations, stated inaccessible from Python and unexposed to C API, are classified private here. Mere underscore, deprecation, experimental status, unsupported implementation, internal usage or opaque storage is insufficient.

UNRESOLVED.rule: Insufficient or conflicting visibility/name evidence retains an unresolved candidate and blocks scope completion; no removal or negative parity credit.

PUBLIC-UNDERSCORE-EXCEPTION.rule: Documented public underscore/C-user APIs remain public even when unstable/version-specific. Two known ufunc members are retained outside this admitted input denominator pending admission rather than classified private.

opaque_struct_policy: Public opaque type/field views preserve accessor, deprecated direct access and ABI restrictions. Internal implementation usage alone never removes their public behavior.
alias_policy: All admitted alias/view identities remain separate. A relation is not a completed equivalence proof or permission to drop framework-specific cases.
tooling_owner_caveat: Finite design exceptions replace the broad COMPAT-LEGACY/Coeus fallback. Proposed native interop/Leto and typing boundaries are not approved owners, code or dependency edges; exact counts belong to ownership-exceptions.json.
